summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 606% YoY to INR811 crore and PAT turned to INR35 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.03% on maize prices up 25-30%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR811 crore versus INR115 crore a year earlier, and up from INR627 crore in Q1, with PAT of about INR35 crore against a loss of INR38 crore. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.03% from a higher H1 level of about 18.2%, as maize prices rose 25-30% during the quarter and raw material was bought at elevated cost. Ethanol allocations were increased during the quarter after a Supreme Court judgment, lifting the last supply year's allocation from 24.5 crore litres to 34.5 crore litres, with a further 5 crore litres reported. Management guided to a shrinking bottom line in the coming year due to El Nino-linked feedstock shortages, while CBG capacity is being added.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Ethanol volumes sold were 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres in H1). About 8.5 crore litres of orders remain to be supplied in October-November, and management expects 6-7 crore litres of additional volume in November-December.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas)
segments.commentary: First 20 TPD JV plant with Sumitomo is ramping up; two more plants are expected in the quarter, taking installed capacity to about 72 TPD from four operating plants. Management expects about INR20 crore of CBG revenue from the two to three plants over the next two quarters.

segments.name: SAF (sustainable aviation fuel)
segments.commentary: Front-end engineering is ongoing and about INR150 crore of viability gap funding has been received under PM JI-VAN for the proposed plant. Capex awaits a government roadmap that has not yet been announced.

segments.name: Fuel retail
segments.commentary: About 7 outlets are operational with more nearing commissioning; outlet expansion is being slowed due to crude price volatility.

guidance_outlook: Ethanol capacity utilisation expected to rise to at least 75-80% on average, from 65-70% in the last supply year; new-year allocation expected at about 40-42 crore litres (one analyst question cited 45 crore litres as the expectation).

Ethanol EBITDA margin expected to dip about 1-2 percentage points on average versus the run-rate once new tenders are allocated; Q2 described as the seasonally weakest quarter, with margin recovery expected from Q3.
Management expects the bottom line to shrink due to El Nino-linked raw material price and availability pressure; intends to forward-buy and stock maize and rice.
Raw material cost as a share of revenue expected to be sub-70% going forward, versus 62-66% historically.
Ethanol gross margin currently about 30% per CFO, which management declined to guide forward.

CBG: expected capex of about INR300 crore for four to five add-on plants at about INR65 crore per plant, with incremental term debt of about INR70-80 crore; GOBARdhan subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD (25% currently receivable) and about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

Badami (Unit 5) slump sale expected to realise about INR170 crore, with about INR125-130 crore of term loan repaid and about INR40-46 crore retained; management expects about INR22 crore annual cost savings.
capex_capacity: Ethanol installed capacity about 2,000 KLPD (about 1,900 crore litres per year industry view); management says all ethanol capex is complete and no ethanol capex is planned next quarter. Three plants converted to grain-based dual feed; one 400 KLPD plant to run on C-heavy molasses/ENA.
Ethanol capacity utilisation was 62% in Q2 at the 400 KLPD plant and about 64-65% in H1.
CBG installed capacity to reach about 72 TPD by end of quarter; plan to start construction of six additional units with GAIL.
Srikakulam SAF plant planned on the PM JI-VAN grant; capex to start only after the government roadmap is announced.
Expected Q3 CBG working capital requirement of about INR25-30 crore at 100 TPD scale; current 10 TPD plant needs about INR2.5-3 crore.
demand_pricing: Maize prices rose 25-30% in Q2; management expects maize availability down about 35% and rice and sugarcane down 10-12% next year due to El Nino.
Ethanol realisation this year: maize-based about INR68/litre, damaged food grain about INR64, FCI rice about INR60; blended average about INR64-65 versus about INR67 last year.
Government reduced maize-based ethanol price by about INR3/litre in the current tender; sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses banned for the 2026-27 supply year.
ENA long-contract prices about INR62-63/litre, with ENA production cost about INR1.5-2/litre lower than ethanol from C-heavy molasses.
DDGS byproduct price about INR26-30/kg. CBG revenue per TPD about INR4-4.5 crore; gas price rises from INR84 to about INR104/kg (up to INR116-120/kg for higher purity) under GOBARdhan 2.0.
Management sees roughly 230 mono-feed sugar-based plants out of about 500 unable to supply continuous ethanol, and the OMC tender demand about 1,100 crore litres.

Chemical/industrial alcohol demand cited at 250-300 crore litres; management expects 40-50% to be met by Indian producers. Industrial alcohol imports (RS) now INR58-60/litre versus INR47-48 previously.

qa_highlights.question: What volume guidance for next two quarters, and what execution risks for the Srikakulam SAF plant and feedstock strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8.5 crore litres of existing orders for October-November; new-year allocation expected at 40-42 crore litres, subject to bids. Feedstock to be sourced nationally (Bihar, MP, Punjab) with warehouses being secured.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and debt plans, and working capital risk from CBG expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No ethanol capex; CBG capex about INR300 crore for four to five plants with about INR70-80 crore new term debt. Working capital need is minimal; CBG subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD reduces term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol volumes this quarter, and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol sold: 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres H1). Margin expected to rise from Q3 with a possible 1-2 point average dip once tenders are allocated.

qa_highlights.question: CBG revenue ramp and subsidy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore CBG revenue expected over the next two quarters from two to three plants; subsidy of about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and raw material cost structure for ethanol and CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize ethanol about INR68/litre, blended about INR64-65; raw material share below 70% of revenue. CBG EBITDA guided at about 50-55% at 20 TPD, against a track record near 60%; revenue about INR80 crore per 20 TPD plant.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory holding and margin sustainability in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory of INR206 crore at September is expected to clear with the new season. Management would not disclose the maize-based realisation for next year before allocations; about 4.5 crore litres remain to be supplied this quarter.

risks_watch: Maize and raw material price inflation and feedstock availability with El Nino; management expects a squeeze on the bottom line in the next supply year.
Ethanol price cut in the current OMC tender (about INR3/litre) and allocation outcome for 40-42 crore litres, not yet confirmed.
SAF project depends on an unannounced government roadmap; no capex has started.
Finance costs rose to INR87 crore in H1 (from INR76 crore), and debt-to-equity is about 0.55x; new CBG term debt of about INR70-80 crore is planned.
Promoter pledge and share purchase intent (stake about 71%, headroom to 75%) and a personal loan were raised in the call; management said it does not affect the company.
Subsidy receipt timing (INR25-30 crore expected by December or January) and the Badami slump sale completion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, utilisation and CBG policy support, but cautious on margins, citing raw material inflation and El Nino. Management was evasive on forward ethanol margin and realisation numbers, saying these depend on allocations, and it deflected a question on promoter personal financing.
